entries.what_happened: Two manuscripts in the family claim the symmetric Mahler inequality, and one of them also claims the equality case. (1) 'The symmetric Mahler conjecture and its equality cases' (OpenAI, dated 22 September 2026) claims that every origin-symmetric convex body K in Rⁿ, for every n ≥ 1, satisfies |K|·|K°| ≥ 4ⁿ/n!, with equality exactly for invertible linear images of Hanner polytopes. The inequality is obtained from a lens-based holomorphic mass estimate, which gives a feasible-simplex sum S ≥ 1; since S = (d!/4ᵈ)·∫|Σ_X| dX ≤ (d!/4ᵈ)·|K|·|K°|, this yields |K|·|K°| ≥ 4ᵈ/d!. The equality case lifts K to K ⊕₁ [-1,1] in dimension n+1, builds representations with lens-minimal cost, obtains metric medians for triples in the polar norm, and applies the Hansen–Lima classification of finite-dimensional spaces with the three-ball property. (2) 'Symplectic Balls in Symmetric Polar Products' (same date) claims that for every n ≥ 2 and every origin-symmetric convex body K, the Gromov width of int K × int K° is exactly 4, and that for each 0 < c < 4 there is a smooth symplectic embedding of the standard ball of capacity c (normalised so a ball of radius r has capacity πr²). The upper bound 4 comes from a supporting-slab construction and Gromov's nonsqueezing; the lower bound from a finite-strip construction plus an approximation in the polar body. Its Corollary (symmetric Mahler inequality, every n ≥ 1, with n = 1 checked by hand) follows by comparing volumes: vol(B(c)) = cⁿ/n! ≤ |K|·|K°|, then letting c increase to 4. This paper makes no claim about equality. (3) 'The Mahler Conjecture for General Convex Bodies' (same date) is also in the family, but it does not address the symmetric problem. It proves P(K) ≥ (n+1)^(n+1)/(n!)² for all convex bodies, with simplices as the equality cases. Its introduction says the symmetric result is a separate companion theorem and that the general bound does not establish it. Its functional and entropy–transport corollaries lie outside this bullet.
entries.delivers: Part (1) of problem_asks, the inequality |K|·|K°| ≥ 4ⁿ/n! for every centrally symmetric convex body in every dimension n ≥ 1, is claimed by two routes: directly by the symmetric paper, and via volume comparison from the symplectic paper's Gromov-width theorem. Part (2), the equality characterisation with Hanner polytopes as minimisers, is claimed by the symmetric paper alone. Its abstract says it resolves the symmetric conjecture 'including its equality classification', so by its own account it settles the problem. Its statement matches the list's: the same polar, the same constant, every n, and minimisers that are invertible linear images of Hanner polytopes. The list's cube and cross-polytope are the basic Hanner cases. Since the product is invariant under invertible linear maps, this is the same class. The symplectic paper's abstract also says it 'resolves the symmetric Mahler conjecture positively in every dimension', but its text claims only the inequality. Its own content is stronger than the inequality. It states the exact Gromov width 4 of int K × int K° for every symmetric K with n ≥ 2, and it claims smooth embeddings of every ball with capacity below 4. It does not claim an embedding at capacity exactly 4. Per the paper, earlier results covered only special families or the upper bound: Artstein-Avidan–Karasev–Ostrover (via a Hofer–Zehnder capacity computation), Karasev for ℓ_p balls, Ramos–Sepe for the cube × cross-polytope, and Vicente for some functional-dual and ordinary polar products.
entries.remains: If the claims hold, nothing in the bullet's problem_asks remains open. Both the inequality in every dimension and the equality classification are claimed. Outside the bullet, the family leaves the non-symmetric problem to the general-bodies paper, which gives the different constant (n+1)^(n+1)/(n!)². The symplectic paper does not claim a ball embedding at capacity exactly 4, and its packing corollary for n ≥ 3 rests on a separate preprint. Neither affects the Mahler statement.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture: the inequality in all dimensions, and the Hanner equality classification in the symmetric paper
entries.object: No counterexample. The extremisers are explicit: linear Hanner bodies, built recursively from centred intervals by ℓ∞ sums (Cartesian products) and ℓ1 sums (convex hulls with the origin). The cube and cross-polytope are the basic cases, and the symplectic paper's sharpness remark checks that the cube has product 4ⁿ/n!. In the symplectic paper the phase-space map on the holomorphic domain is given by an explicit integral formula, but the balls inside that domain are produced by an existence argument (a holomorphic-zero ball theorem plus a compactly supported Moser deformation), not written down.
entries.conditional_on: The equality half of the symmetric paper depends on two cited results it does not reprove: the Hansen–Lima classification of finite-dimensional real Banach spaces with the three-ball (3.2) intersection property [HansenLima1981, Cor. 7.4], and Lima's norm-additive decomposition criterion [Lima1978, Thm. 1.2]. The inequality half is the paper's own argument. It starts from a rotation of Gross's conformal map, and its estimates are proved directly. The symplectic paper's main theorem uses its own finite-strip and approximation arguments, together with standard inputs: Gromov's nonsqueezing, the supporting-slab remark of Artstein-Avidan–Karasev–Ostrover [AAKO2014, Remark 4.2] for the upper bound, Gross's conformal map, and Moser's method. The text says it does not use the companion paper's volume-product or equality results. Its packing corollary alone depends on another preprint, OpenAIBallPackings2026.
entries.doubts: (a) The symplectic paper's abstract and Corollary phrase the volume consequence as resolving the symmetric Mahler conjecture. Its introduction says 'We make no claim here about the classification of equality cases', so it covers only the inequality half of the bullet. (b) The equality half is a chain of cited theorems rather than a self-contained proof. The Hansen–Lima statement uses the term '3.2 intersection property', which the text does not define apart from the three-ball lemma and the citation. (c) The sections I read contain no sketch flags or explicit hedges, and no computer-checked steps. The symmetric paper's inequality and equality arguments are presented as complete proofs. I have not checked them.
